WaitConfig.description:
Explicit browser wait policy applied in order: wait_until → wait_for → wait_timeout.
When a non-null WaitConfig is provided, the adaptive default settle phase is skipped
and the caller owns the full wait sequence. Null fields inside the object are treated
the same as absence of that field.

wait_for.description: CSS selector or XPath expression to wait for before extracting the DOM. At least one matching element must become attached to the DOM for the wait to succeed. XPath expressions must start with `//` or `xpath=`; anything else is treated as a CSS selector. Applied after wait_until.
wait_for.title: Wait For

wait_timeout.description: Deliberate pause in milliseconds inserted after wait_for resolves (or immediately after wait_until when wait_for is omitted), before the DOM is captured. Use to allow late-settling JavaScript to finish rendering. Range: 0–30 000 ms.
wait_timeout.title: Wait Timeout

wait_until.description: Playwright page lifecycle event to wait for during navigation, before the selector wait or explicit delay. Accepted values: `commit` — response headers received and navigation committed; `domcontentloaded` — HTML parsed and DOM ready (no sub-resources); `load` — page and all sub-resources (images, scripts) fully loaded; `networkidle` — no network activity for 500 ms. When omitted, defaults to `domcontentloaded`.

WaitConfig.title: WaitConfig

post.description: Organic Google results, in one shape for every request: `{job_id, query, pages_requested, pages_returned, pages_stopped, pages: [...]}`. `pages` asks for pages 1 to N in one request, fetched through one Google session and exit IP and billed per page returned; without it the answer holds one page. `format` chooses what each page carries: the parsed results (json), the page as Google sent it (html), or both. `ai_overview` adds Google's AI Overview on page 1.

200.description: The pages, page 1 first. "html" and "both" come gzip-compressed for a client that accepts it.

402.description: No active subscription, or insufficient token balance

upstream_blocked.summary: Google would not serve the query

422.description: No page: Google returned no results (`NO_RESULTS`, not retryable: asking again changes nothing), or would not serve the query (`UPSTREAM_BLOCKED`, retryable: the same query often passes on another exit). Neither is billed. A request body the API cannot read is also a 422, with a `detail` list instead of `code`.

As a US buyer sees it, in English. One request is one product, whatever the number of stores.

post.description: Returns the list of URLs found under the given base URL by combining sitemap parsing with HTML link extraction from the seed page. By default discovery is scoped to the exact seed host (a leading `www.` is treated as equivalent) and, when the URL includes a path, to URLs under that path; sibling subdomains and outbound links are excluded. Set `include_subdomains=true` to widen the scope to the whole registrable domain and probe common subdomains (docs, blog, help, support). The optional `search` parameter filters the discovered URLs by case-insensitive substring match — it does NOT query a search engine.
